newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves purchase of Russian fighter planes.
newsitem.headline: India approves purchase of Russian fighter planes.

text.p: The Indian government has approved a proposal by the Defence Ministry to buy an undetermined number of Russia's Sukhoi-30 jet fighters, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
"Yesterday the government approved the proposal and asked the Defence Ministry to go ahead with the negotiations," he said.
A Defence Ministry official said the number of planes would depend on the negotiations.
Last month Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov visited New Delhi amid reports that New Delhi was ready to pay $1.8 billion for 40 of the multi-role warplanes.
United News of India (UNI) said on Thursday that India would buy 20 of the SU-30 aircraft and keep the option to buy another 20.
The Russian aircraft can stay airborne for 10 hours, carry 8,000 kilograms of weapons and fire several types of missiles from 12 points, UNI said.
Last April, the previous government led by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao agreed in principle to make an advance payment of five billion rupees ($140 million) for the planes.
But general elections in April and May delayed a decision.
A Russian embassy spokesman told Reuters he knew nothing about the Indian government's decision.
As the former Soviet Union's main non-communist ally, India was one of Moscow's biggest arms clients.
